sentences.text: Welcome back to the English for Everyday Life podcast.
I'm Emily and today we're going to talk about how to speak English at the gym.
Whether you're a beginner at the gym or you've been going for a while, it's always helpful to know some useful phrases to use when you're working out, talking to gym staff, or asking for help.
In today's episode, I'll guide you through all the important phrases you'll need to feel comfortable at the gym while speaking in English.
One checking in at the gym.
When you first arrive at the gym, you may need to check in at the front desk.
Here are some phrases you can use.
Common phrases for checking in.
Hi, I'm here for my workout.
Do I need to show my ID?
Is there a free trial for today?
I have a membership.
Can I get a day pass?
What time does the gym close?
I'm here for my first class.
Where is the locker room?
Example dialogue.
Hi, I have a membership.
Great.
Can I have your ID, please?
Sure.
Here it is.
Thank you.
You're all set.
Enjoy your workout.
Tip, if you have a day pass or you're trying the gym for the first time, make sure to ask about the gym's policies and hours.
Always ask where the facilities, like locker rooms, showers, or changing rooms are.
Two, asking for help with equipment.
If you're new to the gym or not sure how to use a machine, don't be afraid to ask for help.
Gym staff and trainers are there to assist you.
Common phrases to ask for help.
How do I use this machine?
Can you show me how to use this?
Is this machine free?
Can you help me with my form?
How many sets should I do?
Do I need to adjust the weight?
How much weight should I use?
Can you help me with my posture?
Example dialogue.
Excuse me.
Can you show me how to use this machine?
Of course.
First, sit down and adjust the seat to your height.
Then you can choose the weight.
Great.
Thank you.
No problem.
Let me know if you need more help.
Tip, always make sure to ask for help when you're not sure how to use a machine.
It's important to make sure you're using the equipment safely, especially if you're new.
If you're not sure how much weight to use, start with a lightweight and ask for help.
Three, talking about your workout routine.
Sometimes you might want to talk about your workout with a friend or gym buddy.
Here are some phrases you can use to discuss your exercise plan.
Common phrases to discuss your routine.
I'm doing a full body workout today.
I'm focusing on my arms today.
I need to work on my cardio.
I usually do 30 minutes on the treadmill.
I like to do strength training.
I want to improve my flexibility.
I'm doing squats and lunges today.
I'm starting with a warm -up.
I'm finishing with some stretching.
Nice.
Example dialogue.
What are you working on today?
I'm doing legs today.
How about you?
I'm focusing on my arms and shoulders.
Nice.
We should work out together sometime.
Tip, when you talk about your workout, be specific about the exercises you're doing.
It can help you stay motivated and organize your workout.
For example, you can say, I'm doing 10 push -ups and three sets of squats.
Four, talking about your fitness goals.
At the gym, people often talk about their fitness goals.
If you're working towards something, it's good to express that in English.
Common phrases for fitness goals.
I want to lose weight.
I'm trying to build muscle.
I want to get stronger.
I'm working on my flexibility.
I want to run faster.
I'm aiming to do 10 push -ups.
I want to improve my endurance.
I want to reduce body fat.
Example dialogue.
I'm trying to build muscle in my arms.
That's great.
You should focus on weightlifting and resistance exercises.
Thanks for the advice.
Tip, be specific about your fitness goals, whether you want to lose weight, build muscle, or increase endurance.
This will help you create an effective workout plan.
Five, asking about gym classes.
Many gyms offer group fitness classes, like yoga, spinning, or zumba.
If you want to try one, here are some phrases to ask for information.
Common phrases to ask about classes.
Do you have any yoga classes?
What time is the zumba class?
Can I join the spinning class?
How do I sign up for the class?
Is there a beginner class for yoga?
Is there a class later today?
How long is the class?
Example dialogue.
Hi, is there a yoga class today?
Yes, it's at 10 a.m.
Would you like to join?
Yes, please sign me up.
Great, you're all set.
See you in the class.
Tip, if you're new to a class, make sure to ask if there is a beginner class or a class for your fitness level.
This way, you'll feel more comfortable and not overwhelmed.
Six, after the workout.
When your workout is over, you may want to chat with your gym buddies or staff about how you felt during the session.
Common phrases after your workout.
That was a great workout.
I'm feeling so tired.
I need to stretch.
I think I pushed myself too hard.
I did three sets of 10 squats.
My muscles are sore.
I'm happy with my progress.
I need to drink more water.
Example dialogue.
Wow, that was an intense workout.
Yes, my legs are sore now.
Me too.
I need to stretch before I go home.
Tip, after your workout, always remember to stretch to avoid muscle soreness.
If you're feeling sore, it's okay to take a break and rest.
Seven, gym etiquette.
At the gym, it's important to follow some basic rules so everyone can have a great experience.
Here are a few things to keep in mind.
Key gym etiquette tips.
Wipe down machines.
After using a machine, make sure to wipe it down with a towel.
Don't take too long on machines.
If someone is waiting, don't use the machine for too long.
Respect other's space.
If someone is using a machine, don't get too close.
Keep your phone on silent.
If you need to use your phone, step outside or keep it on silent.
Don't be loud.
It's great to be motivated, but try not to yell or make too much noise during your workout.
Don't leave your weights on the floor.
Always put the weights back after you finish using them.
Tip, be respectful to others and always clean up after yourself.
Follow gym etiquette to create a positive environment for everyone.
That's all for today's episode.
Now you know how to speak English at the gym from checking in to asking for help to talking about your workout and fitness goals.
I hope you feel more confident and ready to practice your English while working out.
If you found this episode helpful, please subscribe and share it with your friends.
Keep working hard, stay motivated and enjoy your workout.
